Wait, there's a problem: I used STATE.PAUSE for both user pause and level-clear transition, and my resume logic is confusing. In the level-clear branch, I set G.state = STATE.PAUSE and setTimeout nextLevel after 700ms. But the user can also press P when state is PLAY only — fine. But during the transition PAUSE, updateFX runs and drawing shows "PAUSED" text overlay, which is wrong. Let me fix: add a separate flag or state, e.g., use a `G.transition` boolean and keep state PLAY but skip updates... Simpler: add STATE.CLEAR for the celebration, and only draw PAUSED text for user pause (track userPaused separately).

Let me refactor: STATE = {MENU, READY, PLAY, PAUSE, OVER, WIN, CLEAR}. Key P toggles only between PLAY and PAUSE. In CLEAR, updateFX + particles, draw everything but no PAUSED text. setTimeout -> nextLevel.

Also the "PAUSED" drawing check `G.state === STATE.PAUSE` only — with CLEAR being separate, good.

Also fix draw hint condition: currently convoluted; simplify: if stuckBall && (state READY or PLAY).

Also in updateBalls, when loseLife is called it sets state possibly OVER or READY via loadLevel+setState(READY). The `return` after loseLife is fine.

Another bug: In loseLife during READY state... can't happen since ball stuck. OK.

In levelCleared check: `bricks.every(b => !b.alive || b.hp === -1)` — good.

Combo popup: addScore shows popup each brick — fine.

One issue: in `updateBalls` clamp speed to target each frame — when slow power picked, speed *0.65 then clamped back to target which includes slowF — consistent.

Another: `applyPower slow` multiplies velocity, then clamp restores. fine.

Edge: ball speed clamp `Math.abs(s - target) > 1` then f applies gradually each frame — okay.

Fix the pause/transition issue now.

## What happened
The previous session was interrupted before any game code was written (it hit a provider usage limit on the very first message — the repo only contained harness/scaffolding files). So I built the full game from scratch.

## What I built: **NEON BREAKER** (`index.html`)
A complete, self-contained arcade brick-breaker — no build step, no dependencies, playable by opening the file in any browser (which is how the OMGithub runtime serves it).

**Gameplay:**
- **8 handcrafted levels** — 1–3 HP bricks (with visible HP pips) plus unbreakable steel bricks
- **5 power-ups dropped from bricks:** wide paddle, multiball, slow-mo, sticky paddle, extra life (with on-screen timers)
- Combo scoring that grows on consecutive brick hits, 3 lives, level-clear bonus
- High score persisted via `localStorage`

**Polish:**
- Particles, screen shake, ball trails, floating score popups, animated neon gradients
- All sound effects synthesized live with WebAudio (no assets) — paddle/brick/wall bleeps, power-up chimes, level-clear and game-over jingles
- Responsive scaling to any window size; touch, mouse, and keyboard controls; pause (P/Esc); menu, game-over, and victory screens

**Verification:**
- Script syntax-checked, plus a headless behavioral test harness in Node (stubbed canvas/DOM) that drives the real game loop — 14/14 checks pass covering: menu → start → launch → play, pause/resume, paddle input, brick/power-up/life logic, level bounds, and game-over reachability.

**Assumptions I made:** since there was no prior game to continue, I chose a polished single-file arcade game as a reasonable default; audio requires a user interaction to start (browser policy), which the Play button handles; and I left `README.md`'s OMGithub attribution block untouched, adding a game description below it.
